speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the right leg weakness and unsteady gait first started? Did these symptoms appear suddenly or have they been getting worse gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see; given the combination of recent motor decline and progressive cognitive changes, have you experienced any headaches, vision problems, or seizures? Also, do you have any history of head trauma or known neurological conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any changes in your vision or headaches, and do you have a history of head trauma or high blood pressure? Additionally, have you experienced any seizures or noticed a change in the strength of your left leg?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of non-compliance with HIV medications, are you currently experiencing any fevers, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss? I also need to know if you have noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder control.

speaker: Patient
text: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast
REQUEST TEST: HIV Viral Load and CD4 Count
REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect. HIV Viral Load: > 100,000 copies/mL. CD4+ Count: 56/μL.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your severe immunosuppression and the MRI findings of disseminated white matter lesions, do you have any history of recent travel to areas endemic for toxoplasmosis or any exposure to cats? I am considering Toxoplasmosis, though the lack of enhancement on the MRI is unusual.

speaker: Patient
text: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of non-enhancing white matter lesions, combined with your very low CD4 count and rapid cognitive decline, strongly suggest Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) rather than Toxoplasmosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
